name: zig-protobuf
notes: Allocation-strategy variant of zig/zig-protobuf: same library, generated code, harness and build flags (ReleaseFast, -Dcpu=baseline, no libc); only the allocator handed to the library differs.

Allocator: std.heap.ArenaAllocator backed by std.heap.page_allocator, created once per dataset. Every iteration allocates its message / buffer from the arena and ends with arena.reset(.retain_capacity): nothing is freed individually (no msg.deinit, no Allocating.deinit, no free) and the arena keeps its memory, so after the first iterations no call reaches the OS.

This deliberately breaks the suite-wide 'fresh allocation, individual release per iteration' rule (docs/METHODOLOGY.md): the column shows what zig-protobuf costs when the caller owns an arena, not a like-for-like comparison with the other libraries' default columns.

json_decode: zig-protobuf has no leaky JSON decode API (Msg.jsonDecode wraps std.json.parseFromSlice and returns a std.json.Parsed with its own arena), so this variant calls the equivalent std.json.parseFromSliceLeaky(Msg, arena, text, .{}) directly; the generated jsonParse code is the same.
Everything else (JSON options, validation, field-order and float-formatting caveats) is identical to zig/zig-protobuf.
